source.title: What Deep CNNs Benefit From Global Covariance Pooling: An Optimization Perspective
source.authors: Qilong Wang; Li Zhang; Banggu Wu; Dongwei Ren; P. Li; W. Zuo; Qing-Hua Hu

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the paper and appendices; no truncation or garbling that prevents reading was apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper experimentally compares global covariance pooling (GCP) with global average pooling (GAP) on deep CNN optimization and convergence, but does not test the training-error outcomes or the specific conditions named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimization-landscape and gradient-predictiveness measurements, plus convergence and classification-accuracy comparisons. These do not measure whether training classification error reaches zero or near zero, so they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study tests global covariance pooling against global average pooling, measuring loss variation, gradient predictiveness and ImageNet accuracy convergence. These results do not test any listed version: there is no training-error endpoint, width intervention, shortcut comparison, initialization comparison, stability-threshold analysis or normalization intervention. References to original optimization studies supply context.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report improved loss smoothness and gradient predictiveness, faster convergence with rapid learning-rate decay, improved distortion robustness and better transfer. They discuss a possible connection to second-order optimization; rigorous theoretical justification remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: The intervention is replacing GAP with GCP, including matrix square-root normalization; the paper compares pooling methods rather than testing the claim's recipes for training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning-rate schedule and covariance-representation dimension affect convergence speed and classification accuracy; the paper reports greater accuracy degradation with faster convergence for lower-dimensional representations.

fits_no_version.finding: GCP produces smaller loss variations and more stable gradients than GAP in MobileNetV2 and ResNet-18, measured along perturbations of first-convolution activations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Replacing GAP with square-root-normalized GCP improves these activation-space smoothness and gradient-predictiveness measurements in the tested ImageNet CNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: GCP with adjusted schedules reaches GAP reference ImageNet accuracy at epochs 68 versus 400 for MobileNetV2 and 32 versus 100 for ResNet-18; completed GCP runs report higher accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested GCP training recipes reach GAP reference accuracy in fewer epochs, with pooling, schedule and sometimes batch size changed together.

record.problems: The optimization-landscape and gradient-predictiveness comparisons are described qualitatively and shown in plots without numeric values in the supplied text. The paper does not report training classification error, and the convergence comparisons change pooling and learning-rate schedule together.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional per-model convergence, robustness, transfer, and computational comparisons in Tables 2 and 4–9. They are outside the claim versions because their measures are classification accuracy, corruption/perturbation robustness, transfer-task metrics, or computational cost rather than training classification error or the listed mechanisms.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels, and dependence on size, stopping and regularization.
Spurious minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction through extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity-shortcut prevention, and the special initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth. Transfer from pretrained models is a different initialization question.
Loss recovery, curvature evolution and divergence relative to the initial or evolving stability threshold. Learning-rate decay experiments do not establish these effects.

Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup. The cited BN robustness comparison does not measure these outcomes.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of numeric plot values does not invalidate the explicitly stated qualitative GCP effects. The row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions because those measures do not test them. Additional results outside the versions are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and the effects of model size and early stopping.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and the effect of student width relative to teacher width.
Training error by depth, plain versus residual networks, and shortcut effects. The paper uses ResNets but does not compare depth or shortcuts as a training-error intervention.
Initialization methods, signal or gradient propagation across layers, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a stability limit, curvature changes, and divergence. The paper varies learning-rate schedules but does not measure stability thresholds or loss recovery above them.
Batch normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training.

rows.subject: MobileNetV2
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss variation along gradient directions for GAP and GCP during ImageNet training.
rows.measure: Optimization-loss variation (Ml); GCP had smaller variations and consistently lower optimization losses than GAP.
rows.note: The text describes the direction of the comparison but supplies no numeric values for the plotted measure.
rows.check: The qualitative reduction in loss variation is explicitly reported, but does not measure any claim version. Appendix I specifies perturbations of first-convolution activations, rather than parameter-space sharpness or a training stability threshold.

rows.subject: MobileNetV2
rows.operation_detail: Trained with GCP under the adjusted learning-rate schedule and compared with GAP under the original schedule.
rows.measure: Epochs to matching accuracy: 68 versus 400; Top-1 accuracy: 73.97 versus 71.58; Top-5 accuracy: 91.54 versus 90.30.
rows.value: GCP + LRadju: 68 matching epoch; Top-1 73.97; Top-5 91.54
rows.note: Measures are ImageNet classification accuracy and matching epoch, not training classification error.
rows.check: Separate the matching epoch, 68, from total GCP training, 150 epochs: the reported 73.97/91.54 accuracies belong to the completed run. GAP trains for 400 epochs. Table 2 also changes batch size from 96 to 192, alongside pooling and learning-rate schedule. These are method-performance comparisons outside all versions.
